title: Example rulesets audit
description:
Triage each example ruleset reference-grade or illustrative, then verify it to the depth its class implies and fix all drift class-wide.

## Background

`docs/examples/` (7 rulesets, 14 files, 1,173 lines) is one of the disjoint-footprint areas in an exhaustive, source-verified documentation audit. TOML schema validity for these rulesets is already covered by the Rust test suite (`crates/jit/tests/example_rulesets_tests.rs:102-108`), so this work's job is narrative and reference accuracy, not schema validity. Recurring drift classes to sweep for include invented CLI surface, stale storage-format specifics, over-credited guarantees, legacy or future narration, and prerequisite/environment drift.

File-footprint signal for the triage: `sdd/` and `research/` are 4-file full-stack rulesets (config, rules, templates, plus a body schema) — reference-grade candidates; `cross-epic/`, `fresh-evidence/`, `nyquist/`, `release-checklist/` are single-file (`rules.toml` only) — illustrative candidates; `bug-repro/` is 2-file (`rules.toml` plus a body schema).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every documented command and flag in `docs/examples/` exists in the current generated CLI schema or the current clap definitions.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every repository-relative link, heading anchor, source citation, and addressable-item citation in `docs/examples/` resolves.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every diagram-shaped block in `docs/examples/` is Mermaid; directory trees and verbatim command output are not diagrams.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every factual claim in `docs/examples/` about CLI behavior, storage layout, repository structure, or engine semantics matches the current source tree; where a drift instance is found, its whole class is swept across the footprint, not patched line-by-line.
- [hard] REQ-05: Prose in `docs/examples/` states current behavior only — no legacy or future/roadmap narration remains.
- [hard] REQ-06: Every volatile fact in `docs/examples/` with an existing projection or citation surface is projected or cited rather than hand-copied; each volatile fact with no such surface is cited to its source file and recorded for follow-up filing.
- [hard] REQ-07: Each of the seven rulesets is classified reference-grade or illustrative with the classification recorded, and audited to the depth its class implies.

## Notes

The linked plan document carries the exact check commands and expected outputs (§2).

CLI-surface verification must use a binary built from the current HEAD; a stale installed binary has previously produced false verification results. The generated CLI schema under-reports the real flag surface (clap `visible_alias` flag forms and the global flags are absent from it), so a documented flag absent from the schema is checked against the clap definitions in `crates/jit/src/cli.rs` before being declared invented; only a flag absent from both is a defect.

No box-drawing content is expected in this footprint on the current tree; any found is adjudicated against the directory-tree/verbatim-output carve-out before conversion.

A doc in this footprint found wholly obsolete or redundant may be deleted or merged into another, with the rationale recorded on this task. Every inbound link tree-wide is repointed in the same change — links are uniformly relative markdown, so inbound references are findable by filename in both bare-name and relative-path forms — and no doc is removed before its inbound links are repointed. After any deletion or merge, every link and anchor tree-wide still resolves.

Blast radius: self-contained to `docs/examples/`.
